Critical Failure: The creature takes double damage, is {@condition sickened||sickened 2}, and takes {@damage 1d8} {@condition persistent damage||persistent poison damage}.

name: Girzanje's March
entries: You sing a prayer for war, inspiring valor in allies who hear your song. Allied creatures who can hear and understand you gain a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, Fortitude saves, and Will saves against {@trait mental} effects.

7: The status bonus increases to +2.
10: The status bonus increases to +3.

name: Gray Shadow
entries: You pray over a {@condition dying} creature, drawing its shadow into your service as long as its owner is stooped at death's door. You summon a greater shadow in a space adjacent to the {@condition dying} creature. The greater shadow has its usual stats (Pathfinder Bestiary 289), with the following modifications:

items: The greater shadow's shadow hand {@action Strike} deals an additional {@damage 1d8} poison damage.

When you {@action Cast a Spell}, you can use the greater shadow's location as the origin point instead of your own location. Upon doing so, the greater shadow immediately disappears. If the {@condition dying} creature targeted by this spell dies or regains consciousness, the greater shadow disappears and this spell ends.

name: Mirecloak
entries: You wrap the targeted creatures in thin, sickly green shrouds that sap information from attackers. The shroud settles about each target's shoulders, granting a +1 status bonus to AC and a +2 status bonus to {@skill Stealth} checks, both only while the target is in dim light or darkness.

If a creature deals damage in melee to or touches a cloaked creature, the cloak wraps around the attacker, temporarily connecting the psyches of the cloaked creature and the attacker and violently prying a random piece of interesting information from the attacker's mind. The attacker takes {@damage 2d8} mental damage and must attempt a Will save. Afterward, the spell ends for the cloaked creature, and the attacker is temporarily immune to mirecloak for 24 hours.

Success: The attacker takes half damage.
Failure: The attacker takes full damage and is {@condition sickened||sickened 1}. In addition, the cloaked creature gleans a piece of information from the attacker's mind.
The details and extent of this information are at the GM's discretion.
Critical Failure: As failure, but the attacker takes double damage and is {@condition sickened||sickened 2}.

name: Stormburst
entries: Your voice projects like cracking thunder as you summon a localized storm, creating a fearsome surge of lightning and wind that deals {@damage 6d6} electricity damage. Each creature must attempt a Reflex saving throw.

Success: The creature takes half damage.
Failure: The creature takes full damage and is knocked {@condition prone}.
Critical Failure: The creature takes double damage, is knocked {@condition prone}, and is {@condition stunned||stunned 1}.

7: The damage increases to {@dice 8d6}, and targets who critically fail are {@condition stunned||stunned 2}.
9: The damage increases to {@dice 10d6}, and targets who critically fail are {@condition stunned||stunned 3}.

name: Swampcall
entries: You call upon the spirits of the soil to twist and churn, transforming the terrain in the targeted area into a sodden mess. The area becomes {@quickref difficult terrain||3|terrain}. Creatures in the area when you Cast this Spell must attempt a Reflex saving throw.

Success: The creature is unaffected.
Failure: The creature sinks partially into the mud. The creature takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds (except for its swim Speed, if any) and becomes {@condition flat-footed}. These effects last until the creature leaves the area or until the end of its next turn, whichever comes first.
Critical Failure: As failure, but the penalty to Speeds (except {@action Swim} speed) is –15 feet.

3: The range increases to 60 feet, and the area increases to a 20-foot burst.

name: Cloak of Light
entries: You surround yourself in holy light that restores the living and rebuffs undead. You glow with bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light to the next 30 feet. Living creatures that begin their turn adjacent to you recover {@dice 2d4} Hit Points. Undead creatures that begin their turn adjacent to you take {@damage 4d4} positive damage.

2: The healing increases by {@dice 1d4}, and the damage to undead increases by {@dice 2d4}.

name: Fear the Sun
entries: You cause the creature's vision to become particularly sensitive. The creature must attempt a Fortitude save. The creature is then temporarily immune for 1 minute.

Success: The creature is {@condition dazzled} for 1 round.
Failure: The creature is {@condition dazzled} for 1 minute.
Critical Failure: The creature gains {@ability light blindness} for 1 minute. If the creature is already exposed to bright light, it immediately becomes {@condition blinded}, as it isn't acclimated to its newly acquired light blindness.

6: You can target up to 10 creatures.

name: Moonburst
entries: A powerful globe of chilling moonlight explodes in the area, dealing {@damage 8d10} cold damage to creatures and objects in the area, plus {@dice 8d10} additional positive damage to undead creatures. Moonburst's cold damage is silver damage for the purposes of weaknesses, resistances, and the like. Each creature and object in the area must attempt a Reflex save.

Critical Success: The creature or object is unaffected.
Success: The creature or object takes half damage.
Failure: The creature or object takes full damage.
Critical Failure: The creature or object takes full damage.
If it's a creature, it's {@condition blinded} for an unlimited duration. If the globe overlaps with an area of magical darkness, moonburst attempts to counteract the {@trait darkness} effect.

1: The cold damage increases by {@damage 1d10}, and the positive damage against undead increases by {@dice 1d10}.

name: Moonlight Ray
entries: You unleash a holy beam of freezing moonlight. Make a ranged spell attack. The ray deals {@damage 5d6} cold damage; if the target is a fiend or undead, you deal an extra {@damage 5d6} good damage. Moonlight ray's cold damage is silver damage for the purposes of weaknesses, resistances, and the like.

Critical Success: The target takes double cold damage, as well as double good damage if a fiend or undead.
Success: The target takes full damage. If the light passes through an area of magical darkness or targets a creature affected by magical darkness, moonlight ray attempts to counteract the darkness. If you need to determine whether the light passes through an area of darkness, draw a line between yourself and the spell's target.

1: The cold damage increases by {@damage 2d6}, and the good damage against fiends and undead increases by {@dice 2d6}.

name: Penumbral Disguise
entries: You wrap the target in shadows, granting them a +1 status bonus to {@skill Stealth} checks to {@action Hide} while in dim light or darkness. In addition, the shadows mask the creature's features. While the creature is in dim light or darkness, other creatures must succeed at a {@action Seek} action against the spell's DC to discern details about the target's appearance.

For example, without using {@action Seek}, other creatures can determine the target's general shape (such as humanoid), but they would need to {@action Seek} to determine the target's precise appearance or any other identifying information.
Creatures with darkvision can still see the target and their features normally. The target's normal appearance is revealed in bright light.

4: The status bonus is +2. Creatures with darkvision can no longer discern details about the target while the target is in dim light or darkness without Seeking, though creatures with greater darkvision can still determine these details.
6: As 4th level, except the status bonus is +3 and creatures without darkvision can't determine even general details about the target while the target is in dim light or darkness unless they successfully {@action Seek} the target; these creatures see a vague shadow instead. Even on a successful {@action Seek}, they only determine general features, though they can see details on a critical success.
8: As 6th level, except the status bonus is +4 and even creatures with greater darkvision must {@action Seek} to discern details about the target while the target is in dim light or darkness.

name: Radiant Field
entries: You create an area of bright light. Creatures with light blindness (Bestiary 343) that are {@condition blinded} by radiant field and remain in the area must attempt a Fortitude save at the start of their turns. On a failure, a creature remains {@condition blinded} for 1 round; this is an {@trait incapacitation} effect. This spell also suppresses magical darkness of your radiant field spell's level or lower.

4: Creatures seen through the area are {@condition concealed} to creatures with light blindness, even those that are outside the area.

name: Wall of Radiance
entries: You form a wall of brilliant light that obscures creatures. You create a thin wall of light in a straight line up to 60 feet long and 10 feet high. You must create the wall in an unbroken open space so its edges don't pass through any creatures or objects, or the spell is lost. The wall stands vertically. If you wish, the wall can be of a shorter length or height. Creatures adjacent to the wall are {@condition dazzled}. Creatures that move through the wall take {@damage 2d6} fire damage (basic Fortitude save) as the concentrated light burns them.

4: The bright light makes it difficult to discern creatures on the other side. Creatures are {@condition concealed} to other creatures on the opposite side of the wall from them. The fire damage increases to {@dice 3d6}.

name: Wall of Shadow
entries: You form a wall of pure darkness in a straight line up to 60 feet long and 10 feet high. You must create the wall in an unbroken open space so its edges don't pass through any creatures or objects, or the spell is lost. The wall stands vertically and, if you wish, can be of a shorter length or height. The wall prevents light from passing through and appears as a sheet of pure darkness to creatures observing it.

Creatures without darkvision or those unable to see through darkness can't see creatures on the other side of the wall. The wall is too thin for creatures to {@action Hide} in the darkness itself, but creatures can {@action Hide} from creatures on the other side of the wall as normal.

5: Creatures with darkvision (but not greater darkvision) can barely see through the wall. They treat targets seen through the wall as {@condition concealed}.
7: Creatures with greater darkvision can barely see through the darkness. They treat targets seen through the wall as {@condition concealed}. All other creatures are unable to see through the darkness at all.

name: Return to Essence
targets: one magically sealed or warded doorway or chest
entries: You unravel the magic of a spell that affects a container, door, or lock, converting it into energy you can repurpose to power your own spells. Attempt a counteract check (Core Rulebook 458) against the target spell or {@trait magical} effect that wards or seals a doorway or chest, such as lock, or against a spell or effect that deals damage or delivers secondary effects when it's opened, such as glyph of warding. If you succeed, you recover its energy, restoring one of your expended spell slots of 3rd level or lower.

8: You can restore an expended spell slot of 4th level or lower.
9: You can restore an expended spell slot of 5th level or lower.
10: You can restore an expended spell slot of 6th level or lower.

name: Temporal Ward
entries: You ward a target doorway or container with a temporal trap that rewinds the personal timeline of creatures trying to open it. A creature attempting to open a warded doorway or container must attempt a Will save with the below results. You can set a password for the ward. Any creature that attempts to open the target container, or to open or pass through the target doorway without speaking the password must attempt a save as normal. The ward vanishes automatically once the spell's duration ends, but can be removed before then as if it were a magical trap, using your spell DC for both the {@skill Perception} check to notice it and {@skill Thievery} check to disable it. Both checks require the creature attempting them to have expert proficiency in order to succeed. You can {@action Dismiss} temporal ward. The maximum number of temporal wards you can have active at a time is equal to your spellcasting ability modifier.

Critical Success: The creature is unaffected and opens the doorway or the container as normal.
Success: The creature experiences a brief moment of dé jà-vu in which they're convinced they already opened the door.

They must use an additional action to open the door. If they can't or don't want to do so, the action or activity they used to open the door or container is wasted, and the door or container remains closed.
Failure: The creature is thrown briefly backwards in time.
The action or activity they used to open the door or container is wasted and they're returned to the position they were located at during the start of their turn. Their turn then ends.
Critical Failure: As failure, but the temporal displacement also causes the creature to lose their bearings, making them {@condition confused} for 1 minute.

10: The temporal ward has an unlimited duration, until it is counteracted, Dismissed, or Disarmed.

name: Glass Sand
entries: You throw a handful of sand that transforms into jagged shards of glass. Creatures in the area take {@damage 4d6} slashing damage and must attempt a Reflex save.

Success: The target takes half damage
Failure: The target takes full damage and 1 {@condition persistent damage||persistent bleed damage}.
Critical Failure: The target takes double damage and 2 {@condition persistent damage||persistent bleed damage}.

1: The damage increases by {@damage 2d6}.

name: Gritty Wheeze
entries: You exhale desiccating grit and sand in a small cloud. Creatures in the area take {@damage 2d4} bludgeoning damage and must attempt a Fortitude save. Water creatures and plant creatures use the outcome one degree of success worse than the result of their saving throw.

Success: The creature takes half damage.
Failure: The creature takes full damage and is {@condition dazzled} for 1 round.
Critical Failure: The creature takes double damage and is {@condition dazzled} for 1 minute.

1: The damage increases by {@damage 2d4}.

name: Nettleskin
entries: Thorns sprout from your body; they pass through and don't damage any clothing or armor you wear. Adjacent creatures that hit you with a melee or unarmed attack take {@damage 1d4} piercing damage as the nettles jab them and break off. Each time a creature takes damage in this way, nettleskin's duration decreases by 1 round.

1: The damage increases by {@damage 1d4}.

name: Frost's Touch
entries: Your gelid shard drinks down nearby heat in a futile attempt to sate itself and achieve a level of frigid cold unheard of on the Material Plane. This allows you to cool a drink, make a hot pot safe to handle, or other, similar minor effects. Once cooled, the object's temperature is subject to its environment as usual. You can also solidify ambient moisture into a solid object; this temporary object is of negligible Bulk, made of non-magical ice. The object looks crude and artificial and is extremely fragile—it can't be used as a tool, weapon, or spell component. Once created, it melts as normal for ice for the ambient conditions.

3: You can create simple objects of ice with up to 1 Bulk and of a level not exceeding 1. Such objects must be rigid. You can only have one such object created at a time; if you create another, the previous object melts instantly.
5: Items you create can be up to 4 Bulk and 4th level.
7: Items you create can be up to 8 Bulk and 8th level.
9: Items you create can be up to 20 Bulk and 12th level.

name: Banishing Touch
entries: Your touch projects a surge of magic that launches your target safely away. Make a melee spell attack at mythic proficiency against your target's AC. If you hit, you deal {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage, and you launch the target into the air and away from you; the target takes falling damage as normal. The number of actions you spend while Casting the Spell determines the damage dealt by your touch and how far the target is launched.

items.name: {@as 1}
items.entry: The target is launched 10 feet into the air and knocked back 10 feet.

items.name: {@as 2}
items.entry: Your touch deals {@damage 2d6} bludgeoning damage instead. The target is launched 20 feet into the air and pushed back 10 feet.

items.name: {@as 3}
items.entry: Your touch deals {@damage 2d6} bludgeoning damage instead. The target is launched 30 feet into the air and pushed back 20 feet.

4: The initial damage increases by {@damage 1d6}, and all distances increase by 10 feet for the 1-action version or 20 feet for the 2- and 3-action versions.
6: The initial damage increases by {@damage 2d6}, and all distances increase by 20 feet for the 1-action version or 60 feet for the 2- and 3-action versions.
8: The initial damage increases by {@damage 3d6}, and all distances increase by 30 feet for the 1-action version or 100 feet for the 2- and 3-action versions.

name: Beseech Arcanotheign

duration.entry: until the end of your next turn

entries: With a whispered prayer or arcane sending, you conjure Arcanotheign, herald of {@deity Nethys|PC1}. She's a storm of magic, half white and half black, roiling in a vaguely humanoid shape. She occupies the space of a {@trait Medium} creature and has a Speed of 40 feet and a fly Speed of 60 feet.

{@b Arrive} ({@trait sonic}) {@i Storm's Unbridled Destruction} Arcanotheign arrives with a flash of light and a cacophonous crash of colliding magic. All enemies in a 60-foot emanation take {@damage 8d12} sonic damage with a basic Reflex save. A creature that critically fails is additionally {@condition deafened|PC1} for 10 minutes.

{@b Depart} ({@trait electricity}, {@trait healing}) {@i Flash of Brilliance} Arcanotheign fires a powerful arcane blast at one target within 100 feet, dealing {@damage 5d12} electricity damage with a basic Reflex save, and a powerful divine blast at one ally, healing {@dice 5d12} Hit Points. Then, Arcanotheign asks for payment in the form of a fond memory. If you pay this cost, you lose this memory, Arcanotheign gains this memory, and Arcanotheign whispers a secret into your mind; you can immediately {@action Recall Knowledge|PC1} on any subject at mythic proficiency.

name: Bounty of the Sky
entries: You call forth a flock of geese that drop restorative fruits and breads from the sky as they fly overhead. You or an ally in the area can {@action Interact|PC1} to collect one of these gifts, and can then either consume it as part of the same action or do so with a separate {@action Interact|PC1} action later in the spell's duration. Enemies who attempt to pick up one of these gifts find that it turns to ash in their hands. Each time a character consumes one of these gifts, they can select one of the following benefits.

items: The character regains {@dice 4d6} Hit Points.
The character reduces the stage of one {@trait poison} or {@trait disease} they suffer from by one stage. This can't reduce the stage below 1 or cure the affliction.

The character reduces the value of their {@condition clumsy|PC1}, {@condition drained|PC1}, {@condition enfeebled|PC1}, or {@condition stupefied|PC1} condition by 2, or reduces two of the listed conditions by 1 each.

2: The amount of Hit Points a character regains from consuming a gift increases by {@dice 2d6}.

name: Final Fate of the Locust Host

duration.entry: until the end of your next turn

entries: You conjure the rotting corpse of Deskari, previously Lord of the Locust Hosts, to the battlefield. Deskari's corpse occupies the space of a {@trait Gargantuan} creature. The corpse is riddled with vermin, including countless locusts, whose collective movement grants the corpse a Speed of 60 feet and a fly Speed of 60 feet.

{@b Arrive} {@i Behold the Rotten Lord} Deskari's corpse is unspeakably foul, emitting a putrid stench, and constantly twitches thanks to the movement of the millions of insects and vermin that consume it. A loud, persistent buzzing is created by the clouds of locusts surrounding it like a haze. Each living enemy creature within a 60-foot emanation must attempt a Fortitude save with the following effects.

Success: The creature is {@condition sickened|PC1|sickened 2}.
Failure: The creature is {@condition sickened|PC1|sickened 3} and {@condition deafened|PC1} for the duration.
Critical Failure: The creature is {@condition sickened|PC1|sickened 4}, {@condition stunned|PC1|stunned 1}, and {@condition deafened|PC1} for the duration.

entries: {@b Depart} ({@trait poison}) {@i Feast of the Locust Host} The millions of insects and vermin feasting on Deskari pour out of its corpse and surge across the battlefield, consuming your enemies. This swarm deals {@damage 5d8} piercing damage and {@damage 5d8} poison damage to enemy creatures in a 60-foot emanation with a basic Reflex save. A creature that critically fails is additionally {@condition drained|PC1|drained 2}.

name: Garden of the Green Man's Growth

duration.entry: until the end of your next turn

entries: You cast your magic into the earth, calling out to a powerful {@deity green man|WoW2}, a verdant lesser deity of nature, to come to your aid. They occupy the space of a {@trait Medium} creature, have a Speed of 40 feet, and a climb Speed of 40 feet.

{@b Arrive} ({@i plant}) {@i Verdant Bloom} The green man erupts from the ground in a burst of lush growth, dealing {@damage 10d8} bludgeoning damage to creatures in a 60-foot emanation with a basic Reflex save. Creatures that fail this save are pushed 30 feet away from the green man and are knocked {@condition prone|PC1}. The area becomes greater difficult terrain for 24 hours.

{@b Depart} ({@i plant}) {@i Forest of Grasping Vines} The green man casts out their arms, causing vines to rise from the ground, lash at up to six different creatures, and coil them up. Each of these vines targets a different enemy within 100 feet of the green man and deals {@damage 12d6} slashing damage with a basic Reflex save. A creature that fails is {@condition grabbed|PC1} until it {@action Escape|PC1|Escapes} (on a critical failure it is {@condition restrained|PC1} until it {@action Escape|PC1|Escapes}). The {@action Escape|PC1} DC is your spell DC. Each creature that begins its turn {@condition grabbed|PC1} or {@condition immobilized|PC1} by these vines takes an additional {@damage 4d6} bludgeoning damage, as the vines continue to squeeze the life from it.

name: It Is Written

duration.entry: until the end of your next turn

entries: You envision a future for yourself, confident in the certainty that this vision is your destiny. Before the duration ends, if you would attempt an attack roll, {@skill Perception|PC1} check, saving throw, or skill check that would aid in the fulfillment of this destiny, you can attempt this roll at mythic proficiency. You choose which roll to use this benefit on before rolling. If you use this benefit, the spell ends. Either way, you're then temporarily immune to {@i it is written} for 1 hour.

name: Part the Mists to Paradise
targets: you and up to 6 willing creatures
entries: You conjure a pathway to paradise, visible only to you and your allies through a dense cloud of magical mist. You and the other targets within range are transported through this mist to an extradimensional paradise of idyllic geographical features. Creatures within this paradise don't need to eat or drink. For each minute you spend within this paradise, all creatures within experience the benefits of 24 hours passing, gaining the healing benefits of a full night's rest, as well as the elapse of any afflictions or spells with day-long intervals. However, for any afflictions or spells with intervals measured in shorter periods of time, only one of those intervals passes for every minute spent within the paradise. This means that at the end of a minute, a creature can attempt a saving throw against a disease whose interval is 1 day, a {@trait poison} whose interval is 1 minute, and a harmful spell that allows a saving throw each round. Each saving throw attempted while within the paradise gains a +4 status bonus.

You and your allies can act normally while within the paradise and can use the time to cast spells, {@action Refocus|PC1}, or perform other {@trait exploration} activities that take less than 10 minutes. When the spell ends, you and all other targets depart the paradise, returning through the mists to your previous locations or in the nearest unoccupied spaces. You can {@action Dismiss|PC1} this spell.

name: Perceive the Threads of Fate
entries: You open your mind to the grand design of existence, enabling you to view the threads of fate in all their complex, tangled glory. You attempt {@skill Perception|PC1} checks and Reflex saving throws at mythic proficiency for the duration.

You can {@action Sustain|PC1} the spell once per round to untangle these threads. When you do, if your next action requires you to attempt an attack roll or skill check, you roll this check twice and use the higher result. You can untangle the threads of fate up to three times. After the third time, the spell ends.

name: Rainbow's End
entries: You reach upward to wrest down a rainbow and harness its power to connect this world to the heavens. Each creature in the area takes {@damage 1d4} spirit damage with a basic Fortitude save. Any creature that fails this save is additionally {@condition dazzled|PC1} for 1 round. For the spell's duration, an ally who's adjacent to you can {@action Interact|PC1} and be instantly teleported to an unoccupied space in the spell's area, as long as they don't travel more than 60 feet. This effect has the {@trait teleportation} trait.

2: The damage increases by {@damage 2d4}, the duration of the {@condition dazzled|PC1} condition on a failed save increases by 1 round, and the maximum distance an ally can use the rainbow to teleport increases by 10 feet.

name: Seize Identity
entries: With a gleeful cackle, you seize an individual's voice and swallow it. For the duration, you look and sound like the target, and the target can't speak. The effects depend on the result of the target's Will saving throw.

Success: You take on the target's appearance, with the same effects of a 3rd-rank {@spell illusory disguise|PC1} spell, and the target can't speak, with the same effects of a 2nd-rank {@spell silence|PC1} spell.
Failure: As success, but the target also takes {@damage 4d6} mental damage from the transformation.
Critical Failure: As success, but the target also takes {@damage 8d6} mental damage from the transformation.

The first time each round you {@action Sustain|PC1} this spell after you cast this spell, the target ages rapidly, taking {@damage 2d8} void damage (basic Will save). On a failure, the target also becomes {@condition enfeebled|PC1|enfeebled 1} or increases the value of its {@condition enfeebled|PC1} condition by 1.

9: The mental damage increases by {@damage 4d6}, and the void damage increases by {@damage 1d8}.

name: Summon Oliphaunt of Jandelay

duration.entry: until the end of your next turn

entries: You briefly summon the mythical Oliphaunt of Jandelay, unleashing a manifestation of pure destruction that obliterates everything unfortunate enough to stand in its path. The summoned Oliphaunt occupies the space of a {@trait Gargantuan} creature. It has a Speed of 200 feet.

{@b Arrive} ({@trait force}) {@i Devastating Displacement} Using hidden magics and long-lost techniques, you conjure an immense gate to Jandelay, compelling the Oliphaunt to step through. The Oliphaunt arrives in a 60-foot burst. Each creature in the area takes {@damage 8d10} force damage (basic Reflex save). On a failure, the creature is also pushed 60 feet away from the Oliphaunt.

{@b Depart} {@i Annihilating Trample} The Oliphaunt becomes aware that it has been summoned to a world that isn't on the verge of annihilation. It summons another enormous gate to Jandelay 200 feet in front of it. The Oliphaunt then rages forward through the gate, crushing everything in its path, before closing the gate behind it and disappearing. The Oliphaunt creates an 80-foot-wide path of devastation that extends 200 feet. Each creature and vehicle in the area takes {@damage 8d8} bludgeoning damage (basic Fortitude save). A creature or vehicle reduced to 0 Hit Points is smashed into fine powder; its gear, passengers, and cargo remain. An unattended object in the area is destroyed unless it succeeds at a Fortitude save, regardless of Hardness, or unless it's an {@trait artifact} or similarly hard to destroy. This trample automatically destroys any {@trait force} effect, such as a {@spell wall of force|PC1}.

name: Diadem of Divine Radiance
entries: You don a diadem of radiant light, which sheds bright light to a range of 60 feet and dim light to a further 60 feet. When you Cast the Spell and when you {@action Sustain|PC1} it during the duration, you can draw a disc of spiraling light from the diadem and throw it at a creature within 120 feet. Make a ranged spell attack at mythic proficiency against the target's AC. This action has the {@trait attack} and {@trait spirit} traits. On a hit, you deal {@damage 4d8} spirit damage, {@damage 1d4} {@condition persistent damage|PC1|persistent spirit damage}, and the target is {@condition dazzled|PC1} for 1 round (3 rounds on a critical hit). The {@condition persistent damage|PC1} isn't doubled on a critical hit.

If the disc passes through an area of magical darkness or targets a creature affected by magical darkness, the disc's glow attempts to counteract the darkness using your {@skill Religion|PC1} or {@skill Occultism|PC1} skill modifier as the counteract check modifier and half your level as the counteract rank.

2: The disc's divine damage increases by {@damage 2d8}, and the {@condition persistent damage|PC1} increases by {@damage 1d4}.

name: Travel by Turtle
entries: You conjure an intelligent sea turtle, who agrees to carry you upon its shell on a water journey. This turtle must be conjured into a large body of water within range, such as a lake or broad river. The turtle conjured is Large, is capable of carrying one {@trait Medium} creature or up to four {@trait Small} creatures, and has a swim Speed of 30 feet. The turtle doesn't engage in combat and doesn't put itself intentionally into harm's way, but it does convey you to a destination of your choice and follows your suggestions. The turtle otherwise functions as a boat, save that it controls itself and doesn't need to be piloted.

5: The turtle's size increases to {@trait Huge}, making it capable of carrying one {@trait Large} creature, up to four {@trait Medium} creatures, or up to 16 {@trait Small} creatures. Its swim Speed increases to 40 feet, and the duration increases to 1 day.
7: The turtle's size increases to {@trait Gargantuan}, making it capable of carrying one {@trait Huge} creature, up to four {@trait Large} creatures, up to 16 {@trait Medium} creatures, or up to 32 {@trait Small} creatures. Its swim Speed increases to 50 feet, and the duration increases to 1 week.
9: The turtle's size increases to {@trait Gargantuan}, making it capable of carrying two {@trait Huge} creatures, up to eight {@trait Large} creatures, up to 32 {@trait Medium} creatures, or up to 64 {@trait Small} creatures. Its swim Speed increases to 60 feet, and the duration increases to 1 month.

name: Trickster's Feathers
entries: You conjure four magic feathers, each with the potential to hold a single illusory guise. These feathers have negligible Bulk and remain potent for the duration. As an {@action Interact|PC1} action, you can place one of these feathers into your hair or cap, or remove an already donned feather. When worn in this way, the feather causes you to appear as another creature of the same body shape, and with roughly similar height (within 6 inches) and weight (within 50 pounds), as yourself. The disguise is typically good enough to hide your identity but not to impersonate a specific individual. This disguise also changes your voice and scent, but it doesn't disguise your mannerisms or behavior. You can change the appearance of your clothing and worn items, such as making your armor look like a dress. Held items are unaffected, and any worn item you remove returns to its true appearance.

When you don a feather for the first time, you determine the illusory appearance that feather grants you, selecting the ancestry, age, gender, attire, and other visual features. For the duration, this feather is linked to that disguise. Wearing it in your hair or hat always imparts the linked appearance. Selecting a feather's appearance for the first time counts as setting up a disguise for the {@action Impersonate|PC1} use of {@skill Deception|PC1}; attempt this {@skill Deception|PC1} check at mythic proficiency.
You can only wear one feather at a time. When you remove a feather, you revert to your true appearance. If you give a feather to another creature, it can no longer impart a disguise.

name: Bee-Man's Summons

duration.entry: until the next time you make your daily preparations or until discharged

entries: You recreate the Bee-Man's infamous ability to sense when someone utters their name. During the spell's duration, you mentally sense whenever someone (referred to as a speaker) speaks your full name while within the spell's area. You gain a vague sense of the speaker's identity, such as "a local farmer" or "a halfling in distress," unless the speaker is someone you have met and interacted with before, in which case you recognize the speaker specifically. As a reaction within 1 minute of the speaker's utterance, you can send the speaker a telepathic prompt, asking if they intend to summon you. If they respond affirmatively, the spell's remaining duration decreases to sustained (up to 10 minutes), during which time you know the direction to where the speaker named you and how far away they are.

4: The emanation's radius increases to 1,000 feet.
7: The emanation's radius increases to 1 mile, and instead of locating the speaker, you can instead converse with the speaker for 5 minutes. This otherwise works as {@spell sending|PC1}.
9: As 7th, except the emanation's radius increases to 5 miles, and the duration of the conversation is 10 minutes.

name: Fungal Exhalation
entries: You exhale toxic mold spores that fill the area. You deal {@damage 6d4} poison damage to creatures in the area. On a failure, a creature is also {@condition sickened||sickened 1}, or {@condition sickened||sickened 2} on a critical failure. A creature that doesn't breathe is immune to this effect.

1: The damage increases by {@damage 2d4}.

name: Hedge Prison
entries: You conjure an intricate hedge prison to trap a creature, encasing them completely in a hollow cube of dense bushes. The hedge has AC 5, Hardness 5, and 20 Hit Points. It's immune to critical hits and precision damage.

Critical Success: The creature escapes the hedge before it fully forms.
Success: The creature is trapped inside the hedge, but the hedge's Hit Points are reduced by half.
Failure: The creature is trapped inside the hedge.
Critical Failure: The creature is trapped inside the hedge, and the hedge's Hit Points are increased by half.

4: The hedge's hardness increases to 7 and it's Hit Points increase to 30.
5: The hedge's hardness increases to 9 and it's Hit Points increase to 40. You can target a creature of Large size or smaller.
6: The hedge's hardness increases to 11 and its Hit Points increase to 50. You can target a creature of Large size or smaller.
7: The hedge's hardness increases to 13 and its Hit Points increase to 60. You can target a creature of Huge size or smaller.
8: The hedge's hardness increases to 15 and its Hit Points increase to 70. You can target a creature of Huge size or smaller.
9: The hedge's hardness increases to 17 and its Hit Points increase to 80. You can target a creature of Huge size or smaller.

name: Mushroom Patch
entries: You cause mushrooms to sprout in the area. The area becomes difficult terrain. When the spell is cast and at the beginning of each round, the mushroom's release a cloud of irritating spores. Creatures in the area must attempt a Fortitude save.

Success: The creature is {@condition dazzled} for 1 round. If the creature moves to outside area, they can spend 1 action to rub their eyes, removing the {@condition dazzled} condition.
Failure: The creature becomes {@condition dazzled} for 1 round.
Critical Failure: The creature becomes {@condition dazzled} and {@condition slowed||slowed 1} for 1 round.

3: The range increases to 90 feet and the area increases to a 20-foot-radius burst.
6: The range increases to 120 feet and the area increases to a 30-foot-radius burst.
9: The range increases to 150 feet, the area increases to a 40-foot-radius burst, and when a creature would become {@condition dazzled}, they become {@condition blinded} instead.

name: Boomerang Shot
entries: You launch a curved length of wood at a foe that arcs around objects and obstacles to strike from an unexpected direction. Make a spell attack roll against the target's AC. This attack ignores the target's {@condition concealed} condition and ignores all cover except greater cover. If you hit, the projectile deals {@damage 7d10} bludgeoning damage.

7: The damage increases to {@dice 9d10}.
9: The damage increases to {@dice 12d10}, and the attack ignores cover completely.

name: Bramble Bush
entries: In a sudden burst of growth, you cause a thorned bush to sprout from the ground, lash around, and wither. Any creature in the area takes {@damage 1d4} piercing damage with a basic Reflex saving throw.
Until the start of your next turn, the area is difficult terrain and hazardous terrain. Any creature entering the square takes {@damage 1d4} piercing damage with a basic Reflex saving throw.

2: The initial damage increases by {@damage 1d4}, and the damage dealt by hazardous terrain increases by 1.

name: Conjured Conveyance
entries: You conjure an intricate vehicle, carved entirely from wood, to serve as a method of conveyance. The vehicle appears in an unoccupied area of your choice within range. The vehicle can be piloted using {@skill Arcana}, {@skill Lore||Driving Lore}, or {@skill Nature} skill checks. The DC to pilot the vehicle and the DC of the vehicle's collision are equal to your spell DC. The vehicle's remaining statistics are presented below.

When you {@action Cast a Spell||Cast this Spell}, choose whether to create a {@trait Large} skiff, a {@trait Large} wagon, or a {@trait Medium} cycle. With the GM's permission, you might instead summon a different vehicle of your choice with a maximum level of 1; this vehicle must be made primarily of plant matter, have common rarity, and be {@trait Large} or smaller.
{@b Large Skiff—Space} 15 feet long, 5 feet wide, 3 feet high; {@b Crew} 1 pilot; {@b Passengers} 3; {@b Speed} swim 30 feet (magical)
{@b Large Wagon—Space} 10 feet long, 10 feet wide, 7 feet high; {@b Crew} 1 pilot; {@b Passengers} 3; {@b Speed} 35 feet (magical)
{@b Medium Cycle—Space} 5 feet long, 3 feet wide, 3 feet high; {@b Crew} 1 pilot; {@b Passengers} 0; {@b Speed} 40 feet (magical)
{@b AC} 13; {@b Fortitude} {@d20 +8}
{@b Hardness} 5, {@b HP} 40 (BT 20); {@b Immunities} critical hits, object immunities, precision damage; {@b Weaknesses} fire 5, slashing 5
{@b Collision} {@dice 2d6}

1: The vehicle's AC increases by 2, Fortitude bonus increases by 2, Hardness increases by 1, HP increases by 20, and the collision damage increases by {@damage 1d6}. In addition, the maximum level of vehicle you can summon with GM permission increases by 2. The duration increases by 1 hour.

name: Cordyceps Command
entries: You conjure a mote of cordyceps spores uniquely tailored to the target before whisking it at them. When you {@action Cast a Spell||Cast this Spell}, choose one of the following behaviors that the fungus compels: ascend, consume, descend, or lure. While the target is {@condition controlled} by the cordyceps toxin's stage 3 effects, it performs that behavior. This control might include risky behavior (such as climbing down a precarious cliff or weaving between armed foes), but it doesn't compel outright lethal actions (such as leaping off the top of that same cliff). If the behavior directly leads to harm (such as falling off the cliff) or {@condition hostile} actions (such as being attacked by creatures that can now reach the descending creature), the target gains a +4 bonus to their next saving throw against the poison.

{@b Ascend:} The creature tries to reach higher altitudes by any reasonable means, such as {@action Climb||Climbing}, seeking stairs, or even stacking debris to jump atop of in an attempt to be as high up as possible.

{@b Consume:} The creature greedily eats or drinks whatever is nearby, using actions to draw and consume elixirs, food, or other consumable items. If the creature has a jaws {@action Strike}, fangs {@action Strike}, or similar unarmed {@action Strike}, the creature can instead chase after and use that {@action Strike} against edible targets. If no other food or drink is accessible, the creature attempts to steal or seek nearby nutrition.

{@b Descend:} The creature tries to reach lower altitudes by any reasonable means, such as {@action Climb||Climbing}, descending while flying, or even falling {@condition prone} and attempting to burrow into the ground.

{@b Lure:} The creature moves toward an exposed location and attempts to get bystanders' attention, such as by gesticulating, Performing, or igniting light sources. The target is {@condition off-guard|PC1} while {@condition controlled} in this way.

Success: The target is unaffected.
Failure: The target is afflicted with cordyceps toxin at stage 1.
Critical Failure: The target is afflicted with cordyceps toxin at stage 2.

name: Reed Whistle
entries: You enchant a blade of grass that you can easily hold in your mouth without inhibiting your speech or other actions. As a reaction, you can reduce the spell's remaining duration by 1 hour to {@action Point Out} a creature you detect as you sharply whistle through the reed. You and your allies also gain a +2 circumstance bonus to {@skill Perception} checks to {@action Seek} the creature for {@dice 1d4} rounds.

3: The spell's duration becomes 4 hours.

name: Cyclone Rondo
entries: Playing or singing melodies discovered by the ancient Shory, you call up a whirlwind. When the whirlwind appears, each creature in its area must attempt a Reflex save or be knocked {@condition prone}. The area of the whirlwind is {@quickref difficult terrain||3|terrain}.

The whirlwind grows harsher when you {@action sustain a spell||Sustain the Spell}, moving up to 10 feet within your range and dealing each creature whose space it enters or passes through {@damage 4d6} damage with a basic Reflex save.

1: The damage increases by {@damage 1d6}.

name: Ki Cutting Sight
entries: Ki flows through everything in existence—animals and plants, living and dead, mortals and spirits. Strike at just the right place, in just the right way, and the flow is stopped with dire consequences.

When you {@action Cast a Spell||Cast the Spell}, make a {@skill Perception} check against the target's Fortitude DC. If you succeed, the next time you deal damage to the target with a {@action Strike} or ki spell, you deal {@damage 4d10} additional slashing damage.

1: The precision damage increases by {@damage 1d10}.

name: Summon Fluxwraith

duration.entry: until the end of your next turn

entries: You break a mirror and cast the shards into the air. Between their thousand fractured reflections, the fluxwraith appears—a thing of broken glass, broken time and broken lives. This {@trait undead} creature occupies the space of a {@trait Medium} creature and has a fly Speed of 60 feet.

{@b Arrive} ({@trait transmutation}) {@i Interrupted Lives} Each enemy within a 10-foot emanation must attempt a Will save. If a creature fails its save, it is shunted into the future, vanishing now but automatically reappearing in the same location after {@dice 1d4} rounds. A creature can attempt an additional Will save at the end of each of its turns to end the duration. If its original space is occupied when it returns, the creature appears in the nearest unoccupied space. Since the creature is shunted forward in time, it doesn't experience any of the intervening time. Likewise, any effects on the creature with a duration don't decrease their duration, resuming when the creature reappears.

{@b Depart} ({@trait divination}, {@trait fear}, {@trait mental}, {@trait prediction}) {@i Dire Foresight} Each enemy within a 60-foot emanation must attempt a Will save. On a failed save, the creature receives a brief vision of a deeply traumatic event that lurks among the many possibilities of its future. The creature is {@condition frightened 2} ({@condition frightened 4} on a critical failure) and {@condition slowed 1} while they are {@condition frightened}.

name: Heinous Future
entries: You hold up a fractured mirror to the target, and in that mirror it sees a thing that may yet come to pass—a ghastly foretelling that the target instinctively knows is eerily possible. It's not a guaranteed thing, just a dreadful possibility, but it haunts the targets's thoughts all the same.

entries.Success: The target is {@condition slowed 1} and {@condition stupefied 1} for 1 round.
entries.Failure: The target is {@condition slowed 1} and {@condition stupefied 1} until it next gets 8 hours of rest.
entries.Critical Failure: The target is {@condition slowed 2} and {@condition stupefied 2}, decreasing these conditions by 1 for each eight hours of rest it gets.

name: Bonewall Bulwark
entries: You create a miniature replica of the infamous Bonewall of Yled, a jumble of bones with threatening limbs reaching from it. The bulwark is 10 feet high, 10 feet long, and 1 foot thick. The bulwark has an AC of 10 and 30 Hit Points. You must create the bulwark in an unbroken open space so it doesn't pass through any creatures or objects, or the bulwark's dimensions are reduced to fit the smaller space. It must pass within 5 feet of you.

The bonewall bulwark grants {@quickref cover||3|cover} from creatures on the opposite side. At the beginning of your turn, you may have the limbs attack a single creature you're aware of within 5 feet of the wall using your spell attack modifier and dealing {@damage 3d10} bludgeoning damage. This ignore cover and {@condition concealed||concealment} provided by the bonewall bulwark.

1: The bludgeoning damage increases by {@damage 1d10} and the HP of the wall increases by 10.

name: Carrion Mire
entries: The ground opens into a seemingly endless mass of corpse limbs, grasping at all creatures within the area to drag them down. Creatures in the area when the spell is cast or beginning their turn in the area must succeed at a Reflex save or fall {@condition prone}. When a creature in the spell's areas would be healed by a {@trait vitality} effect, the carrion mire attempts to {@quickref counteract|CRB|3|counteracting|0} that effect, preventing that healing but not otherwise prevent the effect if its counteracted.

name: Deathless March
entries: You chant a marching song of Yled to empower the {@trait undead} and terrify the living. {@trait Undead} creatures within the area gain the {@condition quickened} condition for 1 minute, which they can use only to {@action Stride}.
Living creatures in the area must attempt a Will save. This gains the {@trait emotion}, {@trait fear}, and {@trait mental} traits for living creatures.

entries.Success: The creature is {@condition frightened 1}.
entries.Failure: The creature is {@condition frightened 2}.
entries.Critical Failure: The creature is {@condition frightened 3} and {@condition paralyzed}.

name: Osseous Cage
entries: You conjure a prison made of bone. Creatures in the space where you create the cage can attempt a Reflex save; if they fail or don't attempt the save, they're trapped within it. The spell automatically fails if the space contains a creature larger than the spell's area.

A creature inside the cage is {@condition immobilized} until it {@action escape||Escapes}, uses an effect that can pass through solid objects, or destroys the cage. The cage has AC 10, Hardness 5, and 10 Hit Points, and it's immune to critical hits and precision damage.
The osseous cage provides {@quickref lesser cover||3|cover} from attacks that pass through the cage, either from the outside to the inside, or vice versa.

2: The spell's area grows by 5 feet on aside and it's Hit Points increase by 20.
